history.period: 1129 CE (present temple); hill claimed as Neminatha's nirvana site since antiquity
history.summary: THIS IS A JAIN TEMPLE, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The foremost of the Girnar Jain temples, a Shvetambara shrine dedicated to Neminatha, the 22nd Tirthankara, who is believed to have attained moksha on Girnar's summit. The present black-granite temple (originally called Karnavihara) was rebuilt c. 1129 CE by Sajjana, governor of Saurashtra under Chaulukya king Siddharaja Jayasimha, in Maru-Gurjara style; it is the largest shrine on the hill (~25,000 sq ft) with 67+ shrine cells around a courtyard. Temple sources claim earlier shrines here dating to the 6th century BCE on a copper-plate inscription - unverified. Girnar is counted among the Shvetambara Pancha Tirth and is sacred to both Shvetambara and Digambara sects. RELATED (not duplicate): seq 289 'Girnar Jain Temples' covers the whole hill cluster; this file covers the specific Neminath shrine.

name: Neminath Jain Temple, Girnar
town_description: Junagadh is a historic city at the foot of Girnar hill in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat. It was the capital of the Chudasama Rajputs and later the Babi Nawabs, and holds Uparkot Fort, Ashoka's rock edicts, and the Mahabat Maqbara. The city is the gateway to the Girnar pilgrimage - sacred to Jains, Hindus, and Muslims alike - with Bhavnath Taleti at the hill's base.
